pointers.sentence: Partials are built on `Parser.extra_data`, new in 5.1: a dictionary in which a tag's compile function may leave data, kept as `Template.extra_data` once the parse succeeds (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).
`{% partialdef row %}` … `{% endpartialdef %}` files a `PartialTemplate` in `Parser.extra_data`, under `"partials"` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:partialdef_func`).
`{% partial row %}` renders the fragment in the context at that point (`django/template/defaulttags.py:PartialNode.render`).
It loads the template before it, and returns the partial filed under the rest (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.get_template`).
The empty name between the dots is looked up like any other part (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`), which the 6.1 notes call "normally a mistake" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The empty name between the dots is looked up like any other part (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`), which the 6.1 notes call "normally a mistake" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
A comment beside the warning says the form becomes an error when the deprecation ends, in Django 2028 (`django/template/base.py:Parser.parse`).
The first release of 6.1 warned for a literal too; 6.1.1 stopped it (`docs/releases/6.1.1.txt`; [Variables and filters: `FilterExpression` and `Variable`](../templates/variables.md)).
Nor does `Parser.parse` look at a filter's argument such as `default:entry..title`, which fails only at render (`django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`).

Each of the decorators `Library.simple_tag`, `Library.simple_block_tag` and `Library.inclusion_tag` now makes the check, and strikes `"context"` (`django/template/library.py:Library.simple_tag`; [Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](../templates/libraries.md)).
The 6.1 notes say only that the undocumented function no longer accepts it (`django/template/library.py:parse_bits`, `docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The 6.1 notes say only that the undocumented function no longer accepts it (`django/template/library.py:parse_bits`, `docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
`{% querystring %}`, new in 5.1, writes a link's query string from the request's parameters and the template's (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`; [The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md)).
Since 6.0 it also takes several positional mappings, in place of the request's parameters, applied in order before the keyword arguments (`django/template/defaulttags.py:querystring`).

A callable that a variable's lookup finds is not called if it carries a true `"alters_data"`; the value becomes the engine's `"string_if_invalid"` (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`).

5.2 set the flag on `QuerySet.create`, `QuerySet.bulk_create`, `QuerySet.get_or_create`, `QuerySet.update_or_create`, `UserManager.create_user`, `UserManager.create_superuser` and their coroutine twins, "to prevent side effects when rendering a template context" (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
A manager's copies of the methods, made with `functools.wraps`, carry the flag too (`django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager._get_queryset_methods`).
The function passes each argument through `conditional_escape` and marks the result safe (`django/utils/html.py:format_html`), so such a call would mark its text safe unexamined.
Since 6.0, `urlize` warns as it links a bare domain: the scheme it gives one, `"http://"`, becomes `"https://"` in Django 2028 (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`).
Django 2028 also removes the setting (`docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).
The 6.0 notes call the setting deprecated, but nothing warns when it is set (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`, `django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).
